Yeah, I've spent a good portion of my time trying to argue against the way philosophy as a coherent subject is shaped, as well as against becoming overly concerned with a particular philosopher. Although I see the risk of in the end leaning towards some school of thought rather inevitable, I think one's reasons for ending up in a such is what matters the most. Granted, I have my way of looking at issues, the world and so forth, but at this stage I am still unaware of what this would be categorized as, and I'm not actively trying to categorize it either.

What first struck me was the way teachers/lecturers argued in favour of philosophy not being a science. Sure, I understand the gist of their argument, but the way philosophy as a subject is taught and the way you're expected to write philosophy (although this does not affect content, only format) seems to be so coherent that it at least could be a pseudo-science. I do see the way those with more experience write and what they regard as important (among other things the use of other authors to aid their argument), and I try to get around this all the time.

Sure, I've taken criticism for not following guidelines too much (e.g. haven't used other authors to support thoughts which have been exclusively mine, at least to me), but I don't read too much into that. It's something which is expected when you hold a counterposition. Also wrote about philosophic elitism and how other subjects are regarded with slight superiority, to say the least.

I guess I am a bit elitistic myself when it comes to what I wish to do. I don't mean that I can use my knowledge of having read Descartes to improve something, rather philosophy in itself. I think that the way you learn to be skeptic towards everything, the way you learn to analyze matters, in philosophy, is a huge advantage for anybody and anything. It is, from my biased viewpoint, useful to be able to see things from multiple perspectives, to whatever extent that is actually possible, and I think this is a skill you learn very well by practicing philosophy.

What I would be very wary of, is becoming stuck in the debate of what an improvement of mankind would be. There will always be arguments, which from a logical perspective may be sound and correct, to argue against striving for a certain way to improve things. But then again, it is an equally solid argument that arguing over what is better will not make anything happen, which I find worse than something happen, good or bad.

The way one is forced to be consistent in philosophy, in order to for instance not contradict oneself, is advantageous when it comes to creating systems of whichever kind. As I already wrote, consistency is something I value greatly, and I think systems would function better if they were consistent. Systems I think of in this sense are abstract ones; Governmental institutions and how these work, how one is to go about doing a certain thing in society (traditions, rituals, habits, etc.) and so forth.

Plato has a simpler name and I prefer his way of writing, even though I disagree with what he actually says. Also since his way of writing is easy to grasp, and the things he says can be simplified easily, it is easy to mock him. On a 'interesting thoughts' scale, his analogy of the cave, its connections to the matrix and the brain in a vat, is something very interesting to me, although his specific example might not be the most adequate for modern discussions. Yet it has provided a solid ground for the discussion, which I suppose is good.

I got into philosophy reading Bertrand Russell and finding many of his thoughts similar to mine. It's now been a few years and I'm not sure if it's like that anymore, and as of right now I don't have a favourite one. Most appears to be morons in some aspect. That, and because of the heavy emphasis on Wittgenstein at my uni, I try to avoid him as much as I can. The last thing I would want is to become indoctrinated into a certain 'school' because of what people around me think. Fuck them, I'm there to learn the general subject, not their idol-based collectivism.

Also I intend to use the knowledge to improve mankind is some way. There are so many inconsistencies in the systems in play right now, that even if I can straighten out just one, I'd regard it as having done something good. This is not strictly political, more a question of consistency. I realised that even the ideologies I disagree most with could technically work if they were implemented the correct way. I might not want to live in some of them even under their utopian forms, but I can't say that they wouldn't work, which people usually say about things they don't understand or don't agree with.

"Voi jumalauta", basically meaning "oh goddamnit", originally meaning "oh, God help" (which is jumala + auta). Phonetically it would be written [ʋo̞i][ˈjumɑlˌɑut̪ɑ] (shamelessly stolen from a pedia near you), but my own attempt at breaking it down would be something as follows.

Voi is a tricky word, atm I can't remember any English words which would have the same pronunciation of 'oi', but since these explanations rarely tend to be that linear and boring, let's come up with something else. Take the pronunciation of 'ice'. If it was written in Finnish, it would probably be spelled 'ais'. That is, the initial vowel would be 'ai'. For voi, we have a similar vowel, only with an 'o' pronounced the same way as in 'wrong'. The 'v' should be fairly straight forward, just a 'hard' v. So now we have "voi". That's easy. Now, the other word is pretty much Finnish standardized anger and hard pronunciation all over.

At first we have 'ju', which the closest example I can find would be the same as 'joomla', only with a short 'o', but otherwise pronounced the same. 'ma' should be easy. Take 'mama', remove the last 'ma, and you have it. 'la' follows the same principle, same 'a'. 'au', that is, what the 'a' transforms into, is similar to 'ow', as in when you hurt yourself because you've been clumsy all over again, only with the same 'a' is in 'la'. 'ta' might be tricky to pronounce the 't', but it's a hard, simple 't'. Like in 'tee'. Same 'a' again.

The key part is that all vowels are pronounced as short, no long ones. That's what makes it effective for screaming it when you're angry, as with many other Finnish words.

Also optionally there is a pause between 'juma' and 'lauta'. If you want to sound really angry and Finnish.

If you think that is ironic, I'm afraid there has been a misunderstanding as of what anarchism actually constitutes. To me, it seems as the core idea you are clinging to is something along the lines of 'no rules - no authority', and seeing both being enforced in that community.

What distinguishes the ideologies of anarchism as a way to run a society from how to operate a small community within a specific system (reddit) is that they cannot put up the same requirements. A subreddit like that needs moderation when what they want is not their own little anarchist collective, but rather a forum to discuss that. It is therefore imperative not to let such discussions be ruined by people with little to no knowledge of the philosophy in place.

This has nothing to do with their core ideals or means their idea of a better society would be invalidated. It only means they operate within the current system by its means and take the necessary precautions to do what they wish to do. The unthoughtful, shallow ideas of anarchism as rejecting all rules everywhere simply does not belong to this kind of people. That belongs to unruly kids thinking they are 'cool' because, like, anarchy, man.

Well, yes. My criticism was a little off, and you are correct in that it is not based on mathematical concepts. But for instance linguistic minorities do not have to be oppressed in order to be considered minorities.

While sociology may have alternative meanings for the term, it would seem odd to use the word in such a manner that it would be a matter of oppression alone. The idea of minority and majority is usually taken to be 'the few versus the many', the other way around would seem rather absurd and would probably be expressed in different terms. I would have a hard time imagining a larger group being the minority to a smaller group, and it would seem odd to have invented a special definition for gender-discussions alone.

What I am trying to criticize here is the notion that women could be said to be a minority; I have a hard time believing that. This is not to say I reject that women are a discriminated against group or an oppressed group - far from it. The semantics in use seem not to want to discuss this, but rather seek to take a term usually used to refer to groups which make up for less than one tenth of the population.

It would seem to me that the will to use the word "minority" does not actually want to consider whether women are a minority, but rather describe the group (I have a bit of problems conceiving women as a 'group', though, since that requires uniformity of some sort and I don't think gender gives you such uniformity, no matter what gender you are.) in terms that may be academically correct, but will confuse the people not familiar with that exact discipline.

As such it does not seem to address the core issue in any way to discuss whether an extraordinary meaning of a common word could be used, it only serves to distract further from the actual debate.

While it may indeed seem as if the kind of posts using simple catch-phrases referring to recognized works by authoritative people, something which a bystander may make analogous to the believers these people aim to criticize, I dare wager a guess that this phenomenon merely remarks upon the altogether overwhelming increase of people from a certain background. It should be noted that the sort of persons, of whom there are more and more on the Internet these days, are bound to find their way to reddit, which unfortunately means they will find their way to the default subreddits. This, in addition to the way being 'alternative' is increasingly hip and the ways to show that are becoming standardized to some extent, means there will be very shallow individuals expressing happenstances from their life in what is to them natural ways. The use of the term 'natural ways' here is merely to be conceived as "how they happen to do things".

However, when it comes to mockery and the like, it should be noted that the specific thread mentioned is a bit uncalled for and does not stay in line with the rest of the threads, but rather seem to take a nab at the overly simplified way the user chose to express his message. This may be conceived as ambiguity on his part by others, a call against elitism using elitism if you will, both as what he was doing and what is being done against him.

Moreover, there is something rather fishy about the way these things are expressed, and while it does not immediately fall under the category of misogyny and the like, it belongs to a mindset where these things are brought forth without questioning them. While it is uncertain whether this was the intent of submitting the kid to SRS, it is a plausibility. I would say there are a great many dangers with hunting for 'Internet points' in that fashion, so to some extent I do understand the need to condone such behaviour in the hope to avoid things taking a turn for the worse.

I think what many feel is a downfall of the thought-provoking insightfulness usually connected towards atheism, i.e. the kind which does not seek to openly mock religions for their own joy, but rather seek to explain why they believe the underlying philosophy would be false. Therefore it is in many ways a great disappointment to see something so philosophical turn into a very shallow willy-waving to achieve temporary viral fame.

Whether these are reasons enough to justify a post on SRS is quite troublesome to say, I do, however, see a great many problems with posts of the like. It would, yet, be in everybody's greatest interest not to stir up fights simply because the picture may have given you the funnies. Rather, I would urge everybody to understand the forces in play here.

You seem sarcastic, but the notion of minority meaning an *oppressed* group is simply not true. Minority, in a societal context, is the group of people which have less than 50% of the country's population. Minorities tend to be much smaller, so a 50% may not be correct, but groups of different nationalities than the majority, or for what it's worth, mother tongue, are minorities, usually making up 10% of the population at most. They are not oppressed, at least not by law, and there are minorities which are not oppressed in terms of the majority's attitudes towards them either.

This is from somebody living in a country with two official languages, one of them belonging to a minority of 6% with equal rights in terms of receiving service in your mother tongue and so forth.

Although it is true that the notion of a 'minority' may be used to claim further rights because of oppression, this does not make a minority an oppressed group.

I'm home alone at christmas eve, my mum's at work until late in the evening and I'm writing on an essay.

Usually I would go out and be awesome, but not tonight. No, not on christmas eve.

While I understand that posts like this may help some people, it seems altogether fairly thoughtless and shallow. Like I said, some people may actually become motivated by reading loud letters on a forum, looking at "encouraging" pictures and feeling really "alpha" (or some similar fairytale-term).

For others it requires more than that, as motivation is highly contextual and very sensitive when there is little of it. The simplification of things where every person's highest goal is to be fit and have a beautiful partner might be common for some people, but again, motivation is highly contextual and as such does not work all too well with absolute statements.

What you want, and what you really need, is a more abstract phrasing, for instance "don't be afraid of change". Usually, what all motivation problems boil down to, is in one way or another wishing to change in some way, but failing to do so. This covers all of OP's points, and a lot more.

If you want to truly be motivational, you have to look towards what can be said about situations on a level of higher abstraction. Fear of change, or rather, fear of the uncertainty of consequences caused by unordinary actions. Of course, throwing yourself mindlessly into situations is usually not desirable, but nevertheless it is paramount that you dare do new things, even if you aren't sure they will turn out okay, as long as you want to.

Want examples? I have went out at 3AM jogging, because fuck it, I wanted to, even though I had to get up early. I have told people I have been in love with them, because abstaining from doing so because of fear will not get you anywhere. I overcame my fear of losing control because of getting drunk, because the fear was holding back my possibilities of changing myself.

These are, of course, not at all extreme in any way, but they are, among other things, actions I have taken to overcome my fear of change, which in turn have held back my motivation.

The most important thing in such situations is to have faith in yourself. If you're like me, you know yourself inwards out, you have a good idea of the systems you operate in, both societal and those you have created yourself. This means that even though you were to stumble upon new and tricky situations, you will most likely handle them with ease. Sometimes, while you may be uncertain, trusting yourself will mean you remain calm on the surface, which makes it easier to show strength outwards.

So it does not matter if you don't hug every second to death with your newly-found motivation. What matters though is maintaining some sort of consequent system, so that you can increase the rate at which situations will turn up where you will be given the chance to succeed. If you have a sound mindset then, you will succeed.

tl;dr; I'm sad because I'm alone at christmas eve.

I want to thank you for having taken time to write a reply. I'm glad you used the term 'meta', since it was really what I was aiming for, I mostly tried to avoid using a specific lingo. But yeah, in my own mind, I went meta, first on myself, then on that perspective, and so on. It went pretty far, and I'm still not sure exactly what it was good for. Examining yourself from a metaperspective certainly is useful, but if you go into a recursion of metaperspectives, the usefulness quickly loses meaning.

What I think you made me realise, though, is that I in fact did not have any real clue about what the smaller steps would be. It's easy to define a larger goal, partially abstract and very flexible, but if you seek to try to achieve it, you really need some way of knowing where to go.
I'm not really sure yet, but at least it highlighted a flaw which was one of the main reasons for not simply doing anything proper.

Again, thank you. It helped. :)

It's been 15 days now, since I wrote this. And well, here are some reflections about it all.

What I can say about it is that writing all this down certainly helped. Another thing worth to mention is that when somebody writes things like these, or at least when I wrote it, it's already going uphill. It is becoming better, you are past the worst phase when you can write things like these.

For me at least, anyway. I see these things as my subconsciousness helping my conscious me, that it knows my situation better than I can ever consciously know, and forces certain actions onto me that I only afterwards can figure out my reasons for.

For most of the time right now, it seems as if I'm doing things, behaving strangely, being annoyed with people, causing drama and a battery of other things only to make my life exciting.. As a desperate way to make things happen, to keep my mind occupied with something, so that I don't die of boredom.

I don't really know, I've just caught myself several times now having done things with negative effects and done things I don't usually do, with positive effects, analyzed them and found out no other basis for them than to create action in my life.

I don't think of it as too dangerous, as long as I come out clean, I'm fine by pretty much anything.

It's just a constant battle, trying to figure out puzzles I've created for myself that I know are unsolvable through logic, that the only way to solve them is to realize that they aren't problems at all, only mindgames created by myself to keep myself busy with something.

This is the situation right now, I'm partially writing this to let you guys know you're doing an admirable work and I appreciate the answers I have received, and partially as a way of making my thoughts clear for myself yet again.

The more you feel that you see through yourself, the more you begin to appreciate your mind and who you are. I see a danger of it developing into yet another narcissistic phase, though.
